final_report:
## Question

Does intermittent fasting improve insulin sensitivity in adults with prediabetes?

Mode: OPEN. Outside lab executable domain. Desk research only. Nothing was executed.

## What is already known

5 verified peer-reviewed sources. All numbers from records.

- [W4400305946](https://doi.org/10.1111/dom.15730): meta-analysis, 14 RCTs, n=1101 prediabetes/T2D. IF vs control/calorie-restriction reduced weight (WMD -4.56 kg), HbA1c (WMD -0.81%), fasting glucose (WMD -0.36 mmol/L), plus cholesterol/triglycerides.
  Limitation: pools prediabetes with T2D; mixes IF protocols and control/CR comparators; no HOMA-IR timing-at-equal-intake contrast.

- [W3098144176](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu12113530) (PROFAST): 12-week 5:2 fasting (600-650 kcal/day x2/week) in prediabetes, HbA1c 43 to 41 mmol/mol, p<0.001.
  Limitation: n=26 completers of 33 enrolled; no non-fasting control; concurrent probiotic randomization confounds attribution.

- [W4387263072](https://doi.org/10.3390/nu15194233): RCT n=72 in impaired fasting glucose, TRE +/- behavioral-economics vs usual care. No significant ITT differences in weight, fasting glucose, HbA1c, fasting insulin, lipids. Benefit only in per-protocol compliers.
  Limitation: small 3-arm trial, adherence-sensitive, short-term surrogates.

- [W4387491927](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.advnut.2023.10.003): meta-analysis 28 RCTs, intermittent vs continuous restriction. Comparable weight (WMD -0.42 kg, p=0.132) and fat mass; slightly greater waist/FFM reduction with intermittent.
  Limitation: healthy adults, not prediabetes; only 17/28 trials energy-matched.

- [W3194089427](https://doi.org/10.3389/fendo.2021.683140): TRE narrative review. Lower fasting/postprandial/24-h glucose, lower fasting insulin and improved insulin sensitivity in a range of trials, but a number of studies found adverse or no effects.
  Limitation: narrative, heterogeneous windows and populations.

Net: fasting-associated glycemic improvement is plausible, with an ITT-null caution. Whether IF improves insulin sensitivity per se beyond weight loss or beyond continuous restriction is not established. No clamp- or Matsuda-specific prediabetes effect, durability, or diabetes-incidence prevention established.

## Hypotheses (agent-generated, untested)

All family `open`, posterior 0.5, zero direct tests.

- Q1: 12-week 16:8 TRE improves HOMA-IR change vs usual timing at equal intake (intake-independent effect).
  Null: TRE-minus-control HOMA-IR difference is zero or CI excludes smallest important effect (15% relative / 0.5-unit absolute, assumption without citation).

- Q2: Any IF benefit is fully explained by greater deficit/weight loss (no independent mechanism).
  Null/reverse: IF exceeds continuous restriction after weight adjustment by >=0.4-unit / >=10% residual (assumption without citation).

- Q3: Apparent gains are confounded/mediated by sleep, late-night intake elimination, activity — not fasting physiology.
  Null/reverse: direct (unmediated) fasting effect persists >=0.4-unit / >=10% with CI excluding zero (assumption).

## Proposed studies (none executed)

All PROPOSED, `executed: false`. Sample sizes and costs are planning assumptions, not observed.

- P1 for Q1: isocaloric 16:8 TRE (e.g. 08:00-16:00) vs usual-timing (>=12-h window) RCT. Same prescribed weight-maintenance diet, equal counselling/contact. 2-week run-in, 12-week intervention. Primary: HOMA-IR change, central blinded assay after standardized fast; clamp substudy corroboration. Comparator isolates timing from deficit. Falsifier: refute Q1 if difference ~zero or CI excludes smallest important effect. Sample ~140 (70/arm). Cost ~$350k-600k, ~12 months.

- P2 for Q2: deficit-matched IF-with-deficit (5:2 or TRE-plus-deficit) vs continuous ~25% deficit, matched prescribed weekly deficit, macros, contact. 12-week loss + 12-week maintenance (24 weeks total). Primary: HOMA-IR change unadjusted plus weight-adjusted and per-kg-lost. Falsifier: refute weight-loss-only if residual survives adjustment >=threshold; support Q2 if differences vanish after adjustment. Sample ~180 (90/arm). Cost ~$400k-700k, ~14 months.

- P3 for Q3: nested objective-behaviour mediation study (actigraphy/CGM/time-stamped diet/accelerometry; late-night cut-off after 21:00 as assumption). Inherits parent randomization, decomposes total effect into direct vs sleep/late-night/activity paths. Falsifier: refute Q3 if direct effect persists >=threshold; support Q3 if adjustment attenuates to near-zero. No new enrolment if nested (parent ~140-180). Incremental ~$150k-300k if nested; ~$400k-600k standalone.

## Critique and escalations

Critic found: Q1 inconclusive with ITT-null warning (W4387263072 tempers Q1); Q2 entirely untested as stated (W4400305946 compatible but unadjusted; W4387491927 off-population); Q3 untested and unmeasured. P1 would falsify Q1 only if isocaloric match and adherence achieved and ITT prespecified; otherwise null is ambiguous. P2 informative but not cleanly falsifying (adjusting for post-randomization weight needs strong no-unmeasured-confounding assumptions). P3 partially adjudicates Q3 (persistent direct effect refutes full confounding under strong assumptions; attenuation cannot distinguish confounding from behavioural mediation). Gaps: no prediabetes-only HOMA-IR meta-estimate; no isocaloric contrast; no per-kg analysis; no mediation data; ITT vs per-protocol multiplicity; clamp-substudy and wearable-wear selection risks; possible trial overlap between meta-analyses unexamined. Cheaper precursor suggested: IPD re-analysis of trials behind W4400305946/W4387491927 plus small provided-meals isocaloric crossover pilot.

Escalations: literature (`lit-review`) — no escalation. Designer (`design-round-1`) — no escalation. Critic (`critique-round-1`) — gate escalated for verification, verdict CONFIRMED: report accurately cites all five sources, three hypotheses, three unexecuted protocols, with numbers from record or labelled assumptions.

Spend: ~$0.35 of $2.00 ceiling.

## Recommended next step

Recorded decision: run P1 first, with P3 nested in it. Reason: information per cost, feasibility, risk. P1 gives cleanest causal test of timing; nested P3 adds mechanism discrimination at low incremental cost. If budget-constrained, do IPD re-analysis + isocaloric pilot before funding full RCTs, and re-justify thresholds and sample sizes from observed variances.

What would change conclusion: P1 HOMA-IR improvement at equal intake with clamp corroboration confirms intake-independent effect; P2 residual vanishing after weight adjustment supports Q2; P3 full attenuation via behaviours supports Q3.

## Limitations

Thin and indirect evidence base. Surrogate outcomes only (no diabetes incidence). Heterogeneous fasting windows. Adherence dependence unresolved. All smallest-important-effect thresholds, variances, and costs are uncited assumptions. No causal identification of timing vs deficit vs behaviour from current record.
